CHIEF COMPLAINT
Second opinion regarding right index finger injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Philip Gutierrez is a 50-year-old right-handed male presenting for a second opinion regarding a right index finger injury sustained during a motor vehicle accident in March of this year, approximately three months ago. The patient was a passenger in a vehicle that was rear-ended multiple times, causing hyperextension of his right index finger. He reports persistent pain and swelling since the injury, inability to make a fist, and symptoms severe enough to affect his ability to drive. He has been treated at Point May Orthopedics by physical therapy and a PA. An MRI obtained on 4/24/2021 revealed a partial-thickness tear of the flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS) tendon with tenosynovitis. He was offered an A1 pulley injection but declined due to previous adverse reaction to dexamethasone causing tachycardia. He sought this second opinion due to conflicting information regarding treatment options. He works as an X-ray technician and emphasizes the importance of regaining right hand function.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies diabetes and rheumatoid arthritis. No other significant systemic symptoms documented.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Adverse reaction to dexamethasone (causes tachycardia)
Adverse reaction to methylprednisolone (causes itching)

MEDICATIONS
Blood pressure medication

ALLERGIES
Dexamethasone (causes heart racing)
Methylprednisolone (causes itching)

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works as an X-ray technician. Right-handed. Drives himself.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Pleasant, cooperative, healthy male in no distress. Regular rate and rhythm, 2+ radial pulses.
Right hand: Swelling and bruising over volar surface of index finger. Normal creases slightly diminished over PIP compared to middle finger. Index finger rests in 10-degree PIP-flexed position. Pain with MCP extension. Paresthesias present. Able to flex DIP and PIP joints with discomfort. Able to make fist. Extensor tendons intact. Collateral ligaments intact.

RESULTS
X-rays (4 views of right hand): No bony abnormalities, intact joint congruency, no soft tissue shadows of concern, no arthritis.
MRI (4/24/2021): Focal soft tissue swelling over right index MCP joint, partial-thickness tear of right FDS tendon, tenosynovitis around FDP and FDS tendons, intact radial and ulnar collateral ligaments, intact MCP joint capsule, intact extensor tendons.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Post-traumatic severe stenosing tenosynovitis of right index finger with partial-thickness tear of flexor digitorum superficialis tendon.

Plan:
1. Steroid injection with betamethasone (Celestone) 1 cc and lidocaine 0.5 cc administered today. Initial attempt resulted in severe painful reaction requiring needle withdrawal. Second attempt successful with minimal bleeding from small palmar vein.
2. Ice and ibuprofen recommended for pain management.
3. Outpatient physical therapy once weekly for 6 weeks with goal of full active and passive range of motion without restrictions.
4. Patient counseled on safety and importance of active finger movement to prevent stiffness, as extensors and collateral ligaments are intact.
5. Reassured that no secondary injury occurred during injection attempt.
6. May require repeat steroid injection.
